Cable longevity

What is the normal amount of time that cables last for you guys? I've had 2 relatively expensive (like 100 bucks, not Abyss gold plated or anything) cables break in under a year (stops making sounds out of one cup unless the cable is oriented in a certain angle/position in both cases). Is that kinda just how cables are, or this should not happen? I was able to RMA one of the cables, so that's good, but while I'm waiting for that the other one broke and now I'm SOL 2

i have never had a cable break on me since i stopped using cheap shitbuds from walmart

I guess it's me

Stock Beyer cable getting pulled on hard almost every day for a year now and no issues at all.

Is this similar to what you have (these are the inputs/outputs I need)? https://www.thomannmusic.com/beyerdynamic_connection_cable_t1_2nd_xlr.htm . Looks pretty nice actually

My Grado 325is with the garden hose cable still work. I’ve had them for more than 10 years now. The cable on my Fostex TH-X00 looks all janky, but it still works after 6 or so years. That’s pretty much it for long lasting headphone cables. I do have some Monoprice RCA cables that are older than middle schoolers 😂

Huh I must just be a bad cable owner

Nah, I have plenty that also broke. Learning how to do the roadie wrap is probably what helped keep my cables going for so long. The not-too-garbage quality ones though.
